statement: The app's commands come from command.Retrieve() (cli-utils), a global --config flag ('path to the config file to use for CLI flags') is added, EnableBashCompletion is true, Name/HelpName default to 'step' (overridable via SetName), Usage is 'plumbing for distributed systems', and Version is step.Version().
sources:
app := cli.NewApp()
	app.Name = stepAppName     // "step" by default
	app.HelpName = stepAppName // "step" by default
	app.Usage = "plumbing for distributed systems"
	app.Version = step.Version()
	app.Commands = command.Retrieve()
	app.Flags = append(app.Flags, cli.HelpFlag)
	app.EnableBashCompletion = true
	app.Copyright = fmt.Sprintf("(c) 2018-%d Smallstep Labs, Inc.", time.Now().Year())

	// Flag of custom configuration flag
	app.Flags = append(app.Flags, cli.StringFlag{
		Name:  "config",
		Usage: "path to the config file to use for CLI flags",
	})

statement: plugin.GetURL maps only the name 'kms' to https://github.com/smallstep/step-kms-plugin; internal/cryptoutil/cryptoutil.go defines the Attestor interface (crypto.Signer plus Attest) and calls plugin.LookPath("kms") for public-key, signing, and attestation operations against step-kms-plugin.
The Go module is github.com/smallstep/cli with a go 1.25.8 toolchain directive.

NewClient in utils/cautils/client.go centralizes online/offline selection: with the offline flag it requires ca-config and returns NewOfflineCA; otherwise it resolves ca-url via flags.ParseCaURL, defaults root to pki.GetRootCAPath(), and returns the online client ca.NewClient from smallstep/certificates.

createNewOrderRequest validates SANs for ACME (email and URI SANs rejected; wildcard DNS names rejected because DNS validation is not implemented), and for LetsEncrypt directories rejects not-before/not-after and always adds the subject CN as a DNS identifier; otherwise it builds a NewOrderRequest with NotBefore/NotAfter from flags.ParseTimeDuration and adds the subject as a DNS or IP identifier if absent.

getAK retrieves or creates an attestation key named after the hex fingerprint of the preferred TPM EK (getPreferredEK); if the AK lacks a valid certificate identity (hasValidIdentity checks the EK key-id URI among SANs) it enrolls with the Attestation CA via attestationClient.performAttestation and stores the resulting chain.

CertificateFlow holds an optional *OfflineCA and offline flag; NewCertificateFlow applies the given Options to the package-level sharedContext flowContext and, in offline mode, requires --ca-config and constructs the OfflineCA.

CaClient in utils/cautils/client.go is the single interface commands use for CA operations: X.509 Sign/Renew/RenewWithToken/Revoke/Rekey/Version/GetRootCAs/GetCaURL plus SSH Sign/Renew/Rekey/Revoke/Roots/Federation/Config/CheckHost/GetHosts/Bastion; the online implementation is the *ca.Client from smallstep/certificates and the offline implementation is *cautils.OfflineCA.
sources:
type CaClient interface {
	Sign(req *api.SignRequest) (*api.SignResponse, error)
	Renew(tr http.RoundTripper) (*api.SignResponse, error)
	RenewWithToken(ott string) (*api.SignResponse, error)
	Revoke(req *api.RevokeRequest, tr http.RoundTripper) (*api.RevokeResponse, error)
	Rekey(req *api.RekeyRequest, tr http.RoundTripper) (*api.SignResponse, error)
	SSHSign(req *api.SSHSignRequest) (*api.SSHSignResponse, error)
	SSHRenew(req *api.SSHRenewRequest) (*api.SSHRenewResponse, error)
	SSHRekey(req *api.SSHRekeyRequest) (*api.SSHRekeyResponse, error)
	SSHRevoke(req *api.SSHRevokeRequest) (*api.SSHRevokeResponse, error)
	SSHRoots() (*api.SSHRootsResponse, error)
	SSHFederation() (*api.SSHRootsResponse, error)
	SSHConfig(req *api.SSHConfigRequest) (*api.SSHConfigResponse, error)
	SSHCheckHost(principal string, token string) (*api.SSHCheckPrincipalResponse, error)
	SSHGetHosts() (*api.SSHGetHostsResponse, error)
	SSHBastion(req *api.SSHBastionRequest) (*api.SSHBastionResponse, error)
	Version() (*api.VersionResponse, error)
	GetRootCAs() *x509.CertPool
	GetCaURL() string
}

statement: step ca provisioner webhook manages webhooks attached to a provisioner (add/update/remove); webhook response data is exposed to certificate templates under Webhooks.<name>, with endpoint flags --url, --kind, --bearer-token-file, --basic-auth-username, --basic-auth-password-file, --disable-tls-client-auth, and --cert-type.

step ca bootstrap downloads the root certificate to <$STEPPATH/certs/root_ca.crt> and writes <$STEPPATH/configs/defaults.json> with the CA URL, root location, and fingerprint, so later commands need not pass --ca-url, --root, or --fingerprint; --install installs the root into the system's default trust store.
sources:
Name:   "bootstrap",
		Action: command.ActionFunc(bootstrapAction),
		Usage:  "initialize the environment to use the CA commands",
		UsageText: `**step ca bootstrap**
[**--ca-url**=<uri>] [**--fingerprint**=<fingerprint>] [**--install**]
[**--team**=<name>] [**--authority**=<name>] [**--team-url**=<uri>] [**--redirect-url**=<uri>]
[**--context**=<name>] [**--profile**=<name>]
[**--authority**=<name>] [**--team-authority**=<sub-domain>]`,
		Description: `**step ca bootstrap** downloads the root certificate from the certificate
authority and sets up the current environment to use it.

Bootstrap will store the root certificate in <$STEPPATH/certs/root_ca.crt> and
create a configuration file in <$STEPPATH/configs/defaults.json> with the CA
url, the root certificate location and its fingerprint.

After the bootstrap, ca commands do not need to specify the flags
--ca-url, --root or --fingerprint if we want to use the same environment.
			cli.BoolFlag{
				Name:  "install",
				Usage: "Install the root certificate into the system's default trust store.",
			},

statement: verify validates a local certificate file (first PEM block as leaf, remaining blocks as intermediates) or a remote address via the shared getPeerCertificates helper, builds the root pool from --roots, and runs path validation with KeyUsages Any.

sign validates the CSR signature, checks that the issuer private key matches the issuer certificate (validateIssuerKey), and requires the issuer to be a CA with keyCertSign; for intermediate-ca the issuer pathLenConstraint must permit the requested --path-len (default 0, -1 for unlimited).

powershell/install-step.ps1 installs step on Windows by downloading step.exe and uninstall-step.ps1 from https://dl.smallstep.com/s3/cli/s3-windows-installer/ into $env:ProgramW6432\Smallstep Labs, adding that directory to the Machine Path, and setting the ssh-agent service to Automatic and starting it.
sources:
$install_dir = join-path $env:ProgramW6432 "Smallstep Labs"
echo "Installing step: '$install_dir'"
mkdir $install_dir >$null

# Determine filename to download
$response = Invoke-Webrequest -Uri "https://api.github.com/repos/smallstep/cli/releases/latest" -UseBasicParsing
$release = $response | ConvertFrom-Json

# Download the binary and uninstall script
echo ""
$exe_file = join-path $install_dir "step.exe"
curl.exe -L -o $exe_file "https://dl.smallstep.com/s3/cli/s3-windows-installer/step_latest_windows.exe"
$uninstall_file = join-path $install_dir "uninstall-step.ps1"
curl.exe -L -o $uninstall_file https://dl.smallstep.com/s3/cli/s3-windows-installer/uninstall-step.ps1
echo ""

echo 'Adding step.exe to the Machine $Path'
$path = [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "Machine")
$path = @($Env:Path.split(";") | where {$_ -ne $install_dir}) -join ";"
[System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", $path + ";$install_dir", "Machine")

echo ""
echo "Enabling ssh-agent..."
Set-Service -Name ssh-agent -StartupType Automatic
Start-Service ssh-agent
Get-Service ssh-agent | Select Name, Status, StartType
echo ""
echo "Please restart shell sessions to pickup path changes."
